course.title: Policy Evaluation Lab

announcements.title: Friday 16 October: our first R lab
announcements.body: Bring a laptop with R and RStudio installed (both free: posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop). Before class, download firms_grant.csv and the Lab 1 script from week 2 and put them in the same folder: we will reproduce the tables of Lecture 2 on subsidised and non-subsidised firms.

announcements.title: How the course is organised
announcements.body: We study policy evaluation through three lenses: firms as targets of public policy (why governments support or regulate firms, and with which instruments), counterfactual evaluation (the methods: experiments, matching, difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, regression discontinuity, synthetic control), and firms as evaluators of their own decisions (pilots, rollouts and A/B tests). Each method is paired with a reference paper, most of them on Italian incentives to firms: you find them in the week where they are discussed and under Resources. Every week has two lectures, on Monday and Thursday, and a lab and discussion session on Friday, run as a seminar: bring a laptop.

announcements.title: Welcome to the Policy Evaluation Lab
announcements.body: Slides, datasets, exercises and exam information are posted here. Slides go up before each lecture; datasets and exercises after it. Bring a laptop to the lab sessions.

weeks.topic: Course presentation; causality and potential outcomes
weeks.summary: Friday 9 October, first meeting: course presentation; descriptive analysis versus causal inference; potential outcomes, the counterfactual and average treatment effects. The three lenses of the course: firms as targets of policy, counterfactual evaluation, firms as evaluators of their own decisions. Software set-up: install R and RStudio.

weeks.summary: Monday: why randomisation solves selection bias; the grant assigned by lottery; does management matter? A management-consulting experiment in Indian textile plants (Bloom et al.). Thursday: what goes wrong in experiments (non-compliance, intention-to-treat, attrition, spillovers, power); Lens 3, firms as evaluators: A/B tests inside companies; exporting and firm performance (Atkin, Khandelwal and Osman). Friday, Lab 2: regression in R and the grant lottery; discussion of the two experiments.

weeks.topic: Part I: difference-in-differences, instrumental variables and regression discontinuity
weeks.summary: The designs as ideas rather than estimators: where the comparison group comes from and which assumption makes it credible. Monday: from matching (comparing similar firms) to difference-in-differences: parallel trends, event studies and staggered roll-outs; Law 488/1992, subsidised firms versus rejected applicants. Thursday: instrumental variables (from the grant lottery to quarter of birth; whose effect we estimate) and regression discontinuity (R&D grants allocated by a score threshold in Emilia-Romagna, an unexpected shortage of funds, the Law 488 rankings). Friday: lab and discussion.

weeks.topic: Part I: synthetic control; reading an evaluation
weeks.summary: Monday: synthetic control: one treated unit, a counterfactual built from a donor pool; from a regional policy to a single large business decision. Thursday: reading an evaluation critically, what it supports and what it does not. Friday: lab and discussion. End of Part I.

weeks.topic: Part II: why and how the state intervenes in the macroeconomy
weeks.summary: The rationale for macroeconomic policy and its political economy: stabilisation, credibility and time inconsistency, rules versus discretion, the incentives of governments. The architecture of economic policy in the euro area: a single monetary policy, national fiscal policies, common rules. How macro policy reaches firms. Friday: discussion and data lab.

weeks.topic: Part II: the new European economic governance
weeks.summary: The 2024 reform of the EU fiscal rules: net expenditure paths, national medium-term plans, the European Semester, escape clauses. Italy as a live case: the excessive deficit procedure and its medium-term plan. Independent fiscal institutions and the Italian budget cycle. Friday: discussion and data lab.

weeks.topic: Part II: fiscal policy and ex ante evaluation
weeks.summary: What fiscal policy does to firms and growth: multipliers, public investment, taxes and incentives. Ex ante evaluation: regulatory impact assessment, cost-benefit analysis and model-based impact estimates by governments and independent institutions. Spending reviews: where evidence enters the budget. Friday: discussion and data lab.

weeks.topic: Part II: the ECB and monetary policy
weeks.summary: The ECB's mandate and independence; interest rates, asset purchases and other instruments; how monetary policy reaches firms through credit and financing conditions. The recent cycle of tightening and easing, and how its effects are estimated. Friday: discussion and data lab.

weeks.topic: Part II: trade and industrial policy in the EU; wrap-up
weeks.summary: Trade policy and tariffs; EU state aid rules and industrial policy; the recovery plan (PNRR) and incentives for firms' investment and innovation. Wrap-up: turning evidence into recommendations for policymakers and managers.

exercises.title: Problem sets
exercises.description: One problem set per method, posted after the corresponding lab. Solutions are released one week later.

exam.intro: A report on a policy intervention of your choice, presented in the last week of the course, followed by an oral exam.

parts.title: Report
parts.description: On a policy intervention of your choice: either an empirical analysis in R with real-world data, or an argument based on explanation and evidence. The policy can be one you assess as successful or unsuccessful; either way, you have to argue your thesis properly, using solid evidence.

parts.title: Presentation
parts.description: You present your report in the last week of the course (week 10).

parts.title: Oral exam
parts.description: Written instead, if the number of students does not allow us to complete the orals on time.
